circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, stretches 5. 281 kilometres and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix as the championship's concluding race since 2009. The venue represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside the Supercars Championship and supporting events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence, meeting the highest international motorsport standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km circuit that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct eras, first as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987 and later as the A1-Ring following its reconstruction and shortening from 1997 to 2003. The track has maintained its role as a significant venue in Formula One racing history through multiple iterations and name changes.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street circuit in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along Baku Boulevard, and at 6. 003 km it ranks as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The venue first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, operated by Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that has hosted the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix annually, marking the championship's inaugural Middle Eastern race. Beyond Formula One, the track accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series, 24-hour endurance competitions, and previously Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple configuration options.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design featuring extensive straights and diverse corner layouts that test all aspects of driver and car performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium, this 7. 004 km circuit near Spa has been hosting motorsport events since the 1920s and featured prominently in Formula One's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has served as the permanent home of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006 interrupting its continuous run as a championship round.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometer Canadian circuit serves as the permanent home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships, open-wheel competitions, and NASCAR events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the country's Formula One grand prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the event returning from 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing championships alongside its restored grand prix schedule.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, serves as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. The venue shared hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch for several decades before becoming the sole British Grand Prix location, and currently also stages the MotoGP British round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km track located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe in 1986. Originally intended as a street circuit in Budapest's main park, the government instead constructed a dedicated racing facility outside the city in just eight months, making it the fastest-built Formula One circuit to date.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The Italian Grand Prix has been held there almost continuously since 1949, making it one of the most enduring Formula One calendar fixtures, while its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" reflects the track's emphasis on high-speed straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course is a 5. 807 km figure-eight track situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, and operated by Honda Mobilityland. With a capacity of 155,000 spectators, the circuit hosts major motorsport events including Formula One and Japanese Super Formula championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating iconic casino resorts and landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas along Las Vegas Boulevard. The track utilizes the famous Las Vegas Strip, which connects many of the city's most prominent hotels and entertainment venues.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez commemorates two Mexican racing brothers who both died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix twice before, most recently in 1992 on a different circuit configuration, and resumed hosting the event starting in 2015 under its current branding as the Mexico City Grand Prix.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 3. 363 miles of track with 19 corners and qualifying speeds approaching 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects Apex Circuit Design, it debuted on the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since become the permanent home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, following city streets around the principality's harbor. Though officially named after Monaco, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its location predominantly within the Monte Carlo area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km circuit that rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021 with the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix. The track hosted the championship for five seasons before the partnership concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, established in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash in 1977. The track operates counterclockwise and features supporting facilities including a kart circuit honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and recently began hosting international electric racing competitions.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 racing facility in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The track hosts multiple international motorsport series including motorcycle racing and endurance championships, while previously accommodating various other racing competitions ranging from touring cars to rallycross events.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a racing driver of Thai and British nationality who currently races for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: A Spanish driver competing for Aston Martin, Fernando Alonso has secured two Formula One world titles during his 23-season career with Renault, accumulating 32 race victories. Beyond single-seater racing, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance competitions, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and multiple prestigious events including two Le Mans 24-hour races, making him the sole driver to have claimed both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight race victories following his entry into the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently drives for Haas in Formula One racing.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, competing at the sport's highest level after progressing through the junior categories.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. He achieved two consecutive runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his Mercedes tenure in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 race victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in prototype racing with Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series. He made seven Formula One race appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a French-Algerian driver competing under France's banner, races in Formula One for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver competing for Ferrari who holds seven world championship titles, equaling Michael Schumacher's record. He also leads in numerous statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his Formula One career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved notable success in endurance racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Monaco in Formula One racing, currently driving for Ferrari. The 2022 season saw him finish as championship runner-up, and he has accumulated nine race victories throughout his nine campaigns in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT's BMW program while also racing part-time in NASCAR's top series. His previous Formula One career spanned from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British Formula One driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 world championship title while securing 13 race victories over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Haas. The driver achieved a significant career milestone by securing victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while racing for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver who raced in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earned the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories over his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who currently holds a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup position for the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch racing driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in Formula One as a reserve driver for Cadillac, making him the sole Chinese competitor in the sport's history. He actively raced in the championship during 2022 and 2024, establishing a unique presence in the series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's works entry until rebranding to Alpine for 2021 to showcase the French manufacturer's sports car division. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025, the squad transitioned away from its longstanding factory team status.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has entered Formula One competition through multiple team configurations, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, is Formula One's longest-standing and most accomplished team, participating continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their emblematic symbol, they remain the sport's most successful outfit by wins and championships.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas, a NASCAR team owner, founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, making its competitive debut in 2016. Ayao Komatsu assumed leadership as team principal in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had overseen operations since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering outfit founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, the team initially excelled in sports car racing before transitioning to Formula One from 1993 onwards. Despite achieving endurance racing success including the 1989 Le Mans victory, the constructor underwent numerous transformations during its F1 tenure and ultimately ceased operations in 2025 as motorsport's fourth-longest-running team by race entries. Audi acquired the organization in 2024 to establish the technical and competitive foundation for its own F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under ownership by Mumtalakat Holding Company. The team competes in the championship under sponsorship arrangements while maintaining its base at the McLaren Technology Centre.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-Benz Formula One team, operating from Brackley under a German licence, has participated in the sport since 1954 in various capacities as both constructor and engine supplier. Currently branded as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, the team underwent a significant ownership restructuring in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff as equal shareholders. The team carries the traditional nickname "Silver Arrows," reflecting its storied heritage in motorsport.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's F1 portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of Red Bull's two teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with facilities near their sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a satellite outfit within the Austrian conglomerate's racing portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and operated by the Red Bull conglomerate. Founded in 2005 and managed by Christian Horner until 2025, the team is one of two F1 entries under Red Bull ownership, with Laurent Mekies taking over leadership following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
